question.text: The conductance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.0015</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> aqueous solution of a weak monobasic acid was determined by using a conductivity cell consisting of platinized <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Pt</mi><mo> </mo></math>electrodes. The distance between the electrodes is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>120</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>cm</mi></math> with an area of cross-section of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. The conductance of this solution was found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi></math> . The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>pH</mi><mo> </mo></math>of the solution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math>. The value of limiting molar conductivity of this weak monobasic acid in aqueous solution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Z</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>×</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Z</mi><mo> </mo></math>is.
